h: Joseph and the Holiness of Eating

p: וְהַתְחָלַת מַאֲמַר יְחֶזְקֵאל:
— And the opening of the statement of Ezekiel (4:14):
"הִנֵּה נַפְשִׁי לֹא מְטֻמָּאָה, וּנְבֵלָה וּטְרֵפָה לֹא אָכַלְתִּי מִנְּעוּרַי וְגוֹמֵר, וְלֹא בָא בְּפִי בְּשַׂר פִּגּוּל".
— “Behold, my soul has not been defiled; neither have I eaten carcase or torn beast from my youth, etc., neither came abominable flesh into my mouth.”
וְדָרְשׁוּ (חֻלִּין לז:):
— And they expounded in Chullin (37b):
"לֹא מְטֻמָּאָה" – שֶׁלֹּא הִרְהַרְתִּי בַּיּוֹם לָבֹא לִידֵי טֻמְאָה בַּלַּיְלָה;
— “my soul has not been defiled”—that I did not entertain sinful thoughts by day to come to nocturnal pollution by night;
"וּנְבֵלָה וְגוֹמֵר" – שֶׁלֹּא אָכַלְתִּי בְּשַׂר כּוֹס כּוֹס מֵעוֹלָם;
— “neither carcase, etc.”—that I never ate meat from an animal people urged to slaughter quickly before it died;
"וְלֹא בָא בְּפִי בְּשַׂר פִּגּוּל" – שֶׁלֹּא אָכַלְתִּי מִבְּהֵמָה שֶׁהוֹרָה בָּהּ חָכָם.
— “neither came abominable flesh into my mouth”—that I never ate from an animal about whose permissibility a sage was asked to issue a ruling.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי אָמַר עַל דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵינָם אִיסּוּר מְפוֹרָשׁ,
— And this indicates that he was certainly speaking of matters that are not an explicit biblical prohibition,
דְּאִם לֹא כֵן מַה רְבוּתֵיהּ דִּיחֶזְקֵאל?
— for if not so, what is the special spiritual distinction of Ezekiel?
וּמַה שֶּׁחָשַׁב "לֹא מְטֻמָּאָה שֶׁלֹּא הִרְהַרְתִּי",
— And regarding that which he counted “my soul has not been defiled, that I did not entertain thoughts,”
אַף שֶׁזֶּה אִיסּוּר מְפוֹרָשׁ לְכָל אָדָם,
— even though this is an explicit prohibition for every person,
כָּתְבוּ בְּתוֹסָפוֹת דְּחָשַׁב רְבוּתֵיהּ
— Tosafot wrote that he counted it as his distinction
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין אָדָם נִיצּוֹל בְּכָל יוֹם (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קסד:).
— because sinful thoughts are among the three matters from which a person is not spared each day (Bava Batra 164b).
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים רוֹאִין אָנוּ
— And in any event we see
שֶׁהִקְדִּים לְתִיקּוּן הָאֲכִילָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה – "נַפְשִׁי לֹא מְטֻמָּאָה" בְּתִיקּוּן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית.
— that he prioritized before the sanctification of eating—the statement “my soul has not been defiled,” reflecting the rectification of the covenant.

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Chullin 37b: “‘I did not entertain thoughts by day…’ One may ask: What was Ezekiel's distinction? Is this not forbidden to every person, as is taught in Avodah Zarah 20b and Ketubot 46a: ‘You shall guard yourself from every evil thing’—one must not entertain thoughts by day that lead to impurity at night? One may answer that he nevertheless counted it as a distinction because Bava Batra 164b teaches that a person is not spared from three things each day: thoughts of transgression, slander, and scrutiny of prayer.”

p: וְהוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקֵּן הָאֲכִילָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה כָּרָאוּי
— And this is because it is impossible to rectify eating so that it is properly in holiness
אִם לֹא מְתַקֵּן מִקּוֹדֶם קְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית.
— unless one rectifies the sanctity of the covenant beforehand.
שֶׁכֵּן הֲסָתַת הַנָּחָשׁ, שֶׁהָיָה לְהַרְגִּישׁ תַּאֲוַות וַהֲנָאַת הַגּוּף,
— For indeed the instigation of the serpent, which was to experience bodily lust and pleasure,
הָיָה מִתְּחִלָּה בַּאֲכִילָה,
— was initially through eating the forbidden fruit,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא נָחָשׁ עַל חַוָּה וְהֵטִיל בָּהּ זוּהֲמָא
— and afterward the serpent came upon Eve and injected defilement into her
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שַׁבָּת קמו.),
— (as written in Shabbat 146a),
וּכְשֶׁבָּא אָדָם עָלֶיהָ נִדְבְּקָה הַזּוּהֲמָא גַּם בּוֹ,
— and when Adam came upon her, the defilement adhered to him as well,
וְנִצְמַח מִזֶּה הַפְּגָם מֵאָה וּשְׁלוֹשִׁים שָׁנָה (עֵירוּבִין יח:).
— and from this sprouted the blemish during the 130 years of his separation (Eruvin 18b).
וּכְשֶׁבָּאִים לְתַקֵּן הַקִּלְקוּל,
— And when one comes to rectify the devastation,
צָרִיךְ לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
— one must first rectify the blemish of the covenant,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ יְכוֹלִים לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם הָאֲכִילָה שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקִּלְקוּל,
— and only then can one rectify the flaw of eating which was the original root of the ruin,
וּלְתַקֵּן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הָאֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה כְּמוֹ קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל.
— and rectify eating to be in holiness as it was prior to the fall.
וְזֶה תָּלוּי בָּזֶה,
— And these are intrinsically interdependent,
כִּי כְּשֶׁמְּתַקֵּן פְּגָם זֶה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַגּוּף בִּקְדוּשָּׁה וְנִקְרָא "בְּשַׂר קֹדֶשׁ",
— for when one rectifies this covenantal flaw so that the body is sanctified and titled “holy flesh,”
אָז גַּם עִינּוּגֵי הַגּוּף בִּקְדוּשָּׁה וּכְאַכִילַת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל.
— then bodily physical pleasures are likewise sanctified, matching the eating of Adam the First before the fall.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 146a: “Why are the nations tainted? Because they did not stand at Mount Sinai. When the serpent came upon Eve, it implanted pollution in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their pollution cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their pollution cease. Rav Aha, Rava’s son, asked Rav Ashi: What about converts? He answered: Though they themselves were not there, their heavenly roots were there, as it says, ‘Those standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and those who are not here.’ This disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, who said: The pollution did not cease from our ancestors until three generations had passed. Abraham fathered Ishmael; Isaac fathered Esau; Jacob fathered twelve tribes among whom there was no flaw.”

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 18b: “Having cited an aggadic statement of Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar, the Gemara cites other statements of his: Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said: All those years during which Adam was ostracized for the sin involving the Tree of Knowledge, he bore spirits, demons, and female demons, as it is stated: ‘And Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and begot a son in his own likeness, after his image, and called his name Seth’ (Genesis 5:3). By inference, until now, the age of one hundred thirty, he did not bear after his image, but rather bore other creatures.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Chaim Yosef David Azulai, Chomat Anach, Yechezkel 4:14: “Our Sages expounded in Chullin 37b: ‘My soul has not been defiled’—I did not entertain thoughts by day so as to come to impurity at night; ‘neither have I eaten carcass or torn beast’—I never ate the meat of an animal that had to be slaughtered in haste; ‘nor has abominable flesh come into my mouth’—I never ate from an animal about which a sage had to issue a ruling. One may say that the kabbalists wrote that the covenant of the tongue and the covenant of the flesh dwell together, and whoever blemishes one is close to blemishing the other. This is ‘my soul has not been defiled’: that he was not defiled at night. And this came to him, beyond his not entertaining thoughts, because he guarded the covenant of the tongue with great care, not eating even from an animal about which a sage had ruled.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: The Chida also reads Ezekiel’s guarding of his mouth and his guarding of the covenant as two linked halves of one verse, since the two covenants “dwell together.” His direction is the reverse of Rav Tzadok’s: for the Chida, care in eating protects the covenant, while Rav Tzadok holds that repair of the covenant must come first and makes holy eating possible.

p: וְאָמַר "נַפְשִׁי לֹא מְטֻמָּאָה"
— And he said “my soul has not been defiled”
נֶגֶד מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא לִי אֱלֹהִים" (תְּהִלִּים נא, יב) –
— corresponding to that which is stated: “Create in me a clean heart, O God” (Psalms 51:12) –
"טָהוֹר", מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא טָמֵא
— “clean”, which implies that an impure heart exists
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סֻכָּה נב.),
— (as written in Sukkah 52a),
וְהַיְינוּ בִּפְגַם הַבְּרִית שֶׁנִּקְרָא טֻמְאָה.
— and this refers to the blemish of the covenant which is designated as impurity.
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ קצב עַמּוּד ב):
— And in the holy Zohar (in this Parashah, 192b):
בְּגִין דְּאִית מִסִּטְרָא אָחֳרָא לֵב טָמֵא
— because from the realm of the Other Side there exists an impure heart
וְרוּחַ עִוְעִים דְּאַסְטֵי לִבְנֵי עָלְמָא וְדָא הוּא רוּחַ טֻמְאָה וְכוּלֵי,
— and a spirit of perversity that leads mankind astray, and this is the spirit of impurity, etc.,
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "נַפְשִׁי לֹא מְטֻמָּאָה".
— and regarding this Ezekiel declared: “my soul has not been defiled.”
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר הַקְּדוּשָּׁה בַּאֲכִילוֹת,
— And afterward he proclaimed sanctity in eating,
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה שֶׁתִּיקֵּן כָּל פְּגָם שֶׁל הַנָּחָשׁ,
— which demonstrates that he rectified the entire damage of the serpent,
וְהוּא נֶגֶד מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְרוּחַ נָכוֹן חַדֵּשׁ בְּקִרְבִּי" (תְּהִלִּים שָׁם),
— and this corresponds to the continuation: “and renew a steadfast spirit within me” (Psalms ibid.),
וּכְדִכְתִיב: "וְרוּחַ חֲדָשָׁה אֶתֵּן בְּקִרְבְּכֶם" (יְחֶזְקֵאל לו, כו),
— and as written: “and a new spirit will I put within you” (Ezekiel 36:26),
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה כְּלָל שְׁלִיטָה לְיֵצֶר הָרָע,
— meaning as in the ultimate future when the evil inclination will have no dominion whatsoever,
דְּעִיקַּר קִטְרוּג הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בָּא מֵאֲכִילָה כְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
— for the primary incitement of the evil inclination derives from eating when it is devoid of holiness.

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52a: “§ Rabbi Avira, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, taught: The evil inclination has seven names. The Holy One, Blessed be He, called it evil, as it is stated: ‘For the inclination of a man’s heart is evil from his youth’ (Genesis 8:21). Moses called it uncircumcised, as it is stated: ‘And circumcise the foreskin of your hearts’ (Deuteronomy 10:16). David called it impure, as it is stated: ‘Create for me a pure heart, O God’ (Psalms 51:12); by inference, there is an impure heart that is the evil inclination.”

p: וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ,
— And this is the overarching theme of this parashah,
שֶׁנִּמְצָא בָּהּ כָּל הַפְּגָם וְתִיקּוּן הַפְּגָם
— wherein are contained both the entire blemish and the rectification of the blemish
מִיּוֹסֵף וִיהוּדָה וּכְלַל הַשְּׁבָטִים.
— concerning Joseph, Judah, and all the tribes.
וּמַתְחִיל: "וַיָּבֵא יוֹסֵף אֶת דִּבָּתָם רָעָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לז, ב),
— And it commences: “And Joseph brought evil report of them” (Genesis 37:2),
דְּאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פד, ז) שֶׁאָמַר:
— for it is stated in Bereishit Rabbah (84:7) that he said:
חֲשׁוּדִין הֵן בָּנֶיךָ עַל אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי,
— “Your sons are suspect regarding a limb torn from a living animal,”
וְהִיא הָאֲכִילָה הַנֶּאֱסֶרֶת לִבְנֵי נֹחַ,
— which is the foundational eating forbidden to the Noahides,
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ אֲכִילַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע שֶׁהוּזְהַר אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּפֵירוּשׁ עָלֶיהָ.
— and it mirrors the eating of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil concerning which Adam the First was explicitly warned.
וְכֵן "תּוֹלִין הֵן עֵינֵיהֶם בִּבְנוֹת הָאָרֶץ",
— And likewise “they cast their eyes upon the daughters of the land,”
שֶׁנִּדְמָה לוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם פְּגָם זֶה מִזּוּהֲמָא שֶׁהֵטִיל הַנָּחָשׁ.
— where he imagined that they harbored this covenantal defect stemming from the serpent's contamination.
וּבִמְכִירַת יוֹסֵף כְּתִיב: "וַיֵּשְׁבוּ לֶאֱכָל לֶחֶם" (שָׁם לז, כה),
— And regarding the sale of Joseph it is written: “And they sat down to eat bread” (ibid. 37:25),
וְאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פד, יז):
— and it is stated in Bereishit Rabbah (84:17):
עֲבֵירָתָן שֶׁל שְׁבָטִים וְכוּלֵי,
— the transgression of the tribes, etc.,
"לֶאֱכָל לֶחֶם" – מַאֲכִיל לֶחֶם לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם.
— through “to eat bread” Joseph became the provider feeding bread to all inhabitants of the world.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהֻקְשָׁה לְהַמִּדְרַשׁ רַבָּה:
— And this means that Midrash Rabbah was troubled:
לָמָּה מַזְכִּיר הַפָּסוּק שֶׁיָּשְׁבוּ לֶאֱכוֹל לֶחֶם,
— why does Scripture explicitly mention that they sat down to eat bread,
וְנַעֲשָׂה מִזֶּה פָּסוּק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד?
— making of this an eternal verse in the words of the Torah forever?
אַךְ עִנְיַן הַכָּתוּב הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ
— However, the inner matter of the verse is as we noted
בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּמְדְרַשׁ רַבָּה:
— concerning what is written in Midrash Rabbah:
אָמְרוּ נֵלֵךְ וְנִתְפּוֹס דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, כְּנַעַן שֶׁחָטָא לֹא לְעֶבֶד נִתְקַלֵּל וְכוּלֵי,
— they said: “Let us adopt the customary way of the world: did not Canaan who sinned receive the curse of enslavement, etc.,”
שֶׁהוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעִיקַּר עַבְדוּת בָּא מִפְּגָם זֶה.
— which is because enslavement primarily stems from this covenantal blemish.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 84:7: “‘Joseph, seventeen years old…’ – and you say he was a lad? It is because he would perform the actions of a lad – he would groom his eyes, lift his heels, and curl his hair. ‘Was herding…Joseph brought evil report of them to their father’ – what did he say? Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda, and Rabbi Shimon: Rabbi Meir says: Your sons are suspected of eating the limb of a living animal. Rabbi Shimon says: They are directing their glances at the girls of the land. Rabbi Yehuda says: They are demeaning the sons of the maidservants and calling them slaves. Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon said: He was punished for all three of them. ‘Balance and scales of justice are the Lord’s’ (Proverbs 16:11) – the Holy One blessed be He said to him: ‘You said: Your sons are suspected of eating the limb of a living animal; as you live, even at their time of corruption, they will slaughter and only then will they eat’ – ‘and slaughtered a goat’ (Genesis 37:31). ‘You said: They are demeaning the sons of the maidservants and calling them slaves’ – ‘Joseph was sold as a slave’ (Psalms 105:17). ‘You said: They are directing their glances at the girls of the land; as you live, I will incite the bear against you’ – ‘His master’s wife cast her eyes (upon Joseph, and she said: Lie with me)’ (Genesis 39:7).”

Rather, see what the Holy One blessed be He prepared for that righteous one at that moment: Sacks filled with spices, so that the wind would blow through them (and provide a pleasant smell) to counteract the odor of the Arabs. ‘Judah said to his brothers: What profit is it if we kill our brother and conceal his blood’ (Genesis 37:26). ‘Judah said to his brothers…’ – Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai said: The verse is speaking in praise of Judah. In three places, Judah spoke before his brothers and they crowned him king over them. ‘Judah said to his brothers’; ‘Judah and his brothers came (.…And Judah said)’ (Genesis 44:14); ‘Judah approached him (and said)’ (Genesis 44:18). ‘Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let our hand not be upon him, for he is our brother, our own flesh. His brothers heeded him’ (Genesis 37:27). ‘Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites’ – they said: Let us adopt the way of the world. Canaan, who sinned, was he not cursed to be a slave? This one, too, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites. ‘His brothers heeded him.’”

p: וְיוֹסֵף אָמַר עֲלֵיהֶם שֶׁהֵם מְקוּלְקָלִים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בַּאֲכִילָה וּבִפְגָם זֶה;
— And Joseph had reported about them that they were corrupted, Heaven forbid, in eating and in this covenantal defect;
וַאֲכִילַת אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי יֵשׁ תֵּירוּצִים בַּסְּפָרִים
— and regarding eating a limb from a living animal, reconciliations are provided in the holy books,
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר שֶׁתּוֹלִין עֵינֵיהֶם וְכוּלֵי, מִסְּתָמָא טָעָה וְנִדְמָה לוֹ כֵּן.
— and regarding his claim that they cast their eyes, etc., he evidently erred and it merely appeared so to him.
וְהֵם יָדְעוּ בְּעַצְמָם שֶׁהֵם נְקִיִּים בָּזֶה,
— While the brothers knew within themselves that they were pristine in this,
וְסָבְרוּ שֶׁמִּסְּתָמָא יוֹסֵף מְקוּלְקָל בָּזֶה
— and concluded that Joseph was presumably the one corrupted in this
וְעַל כֵּן בְּמוּמוֹ פּוֹסֵל,
— and was therefore invalidating others with his own moral flaw,
וְסָבְרוּ שֶׁהוּא הַפְּסוֹלֶת שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
— supposing that he represented the discarded spiritual dross of Jacob, Heaven forbid.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּכְתַּב "וַיֵּשְׁבוּ לֶאֱכָל לֶחֶם",
— And this is why it was recorded: “And they sat down to eat bread”:
שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁלְּפִי דַּעְתָּם פֵּירְשׁוּ הַפְּסוֹלֶת מֵהֶם וְתִקְּנוּ הַפְּגָם לְפִי דַּעְתָּם,
— for since in their estimation they had separated the dross from themselves and rectified the flaw,
יָשְׁבוּ לֶאֱכוֹל לֶחֶם – אֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
— they sat down to eat bread—eating in sanctity,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחֲמִי" (מִשְׁלֵי ט, ה),
— along the lines of the verse: “Come, eat of my bread” (Proverbs 9:5),
שֶׁמֵּאַחַר שֶׁמְּתַקְּנִים פְּגָם זֶה יְכוֹלִים לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם הָאֲכִילָה גַּם כֵּן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הָאֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
— for once this covenantal blemish is rectified, one is empowered to rectify the defect of eating as well so that eating is in holiness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ גַּבֵּי יְחֶזְקֵאל.
— just as we noted regarding the prophet Ezekiel.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Shevat 1:1: “‘He made the letter tzadi rule over swallowing,’ for the serpent’s first enticement was through eating, to experience bodily pleasure in it. From this the serpent came upon Chavah and cast filth into her, as the Gemara states (Shabbat 146a), and from this branched out the hundred and thirty years. … The work of this month is to bring holiness into eating, as it says, ‘The righteous one eats to satisfy his soul.’ … The power of Asher is that he repairs eating and brings holiness into it, as it says, ‘From Asher, rich is his bread (lachmo)’: lechem with a vav, the letter of truth, which is Torah, as is known. Eating is the root of the blemish from the serpent, which caused the blemish of the covenant, as we said. And Asher brings holiness into eating so that it becomes words of Torah: ‘Come, eat of my bread.’”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Rav Tzadok here also traces the blemish of the covenant back to the serpent’s first enticement through eating. He also reads “Come, eat of my bread” as eating that has been made holy and become words of Torah, the same verse he applies to the brothers’ meal. The month of Shevat and the tribe of Asher are named there as the time and the power for this repair.

p: וּבֶאֱמֶת, אַחַר שֶׁיָּרַד יוֹסֵף לְמִצְרַיִם
— And in ultimate truth, after Joseph descended to Egypt
וְנִתְבָּרֵר בַּנִּסָּיוֹן שֶׁגָּדַר אֶת הָעֶרְוָה
— and was vindicated through the trial of Potiphar's wife, walling off sexual immorality,
וְנַעֲשָׂה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם,
— becoming the supernal chariot for the attribute of Tzaddik, Foundation of the World,
זָכָה לִהְיוֹת כַּלְכֹּל
— he merited to be called Kalkol
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ט, א),
— (as written in Vayikra Rabbah 9:1),
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיְכַלְכֵּל יוֹסֵף" (בְּרֵאשִׁית מז, יב).
— as it is stated: “And Joseph nourished (vaykhalkel)” (Genesis 47:12).
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרַשׁ רַבָּה:
— And this is what they taught in Midrash Rabbah:
"לֶאֱכָל לֶחֶם" – מַאֲכִיל לֶחֶם לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם,
— through “to eat bread” he became the feeder of bread to all inhabitants of the earth,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי תִּיקּוּן מִדָּה זוֹ בְּחִינַת צַדִּיק
— for through the rectification of this attribute of Tzaddik
זוֹכִין לְהַאֲכִיל לֶחֶם – אֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה לְכָל הָעוֹלָם.
— one merits to dispense bread—sacred eating in holiness—unto the entire world.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא בַּפָּרָשָׁה עִנְיַן עֵר וְאוֹנָן וְהַתִּיקּוּן שֶׁלָּהֶם שֶׁבָּאוּ אַחַר כָּךְ בְּפֶרֶץ וְזֶרַח,
— And afterward follows in the parashah the episode of Er and Onan and their rectification returning later in Peretz and Zerach,
שֶׁהוּא אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ שֶׁיְּתַקֵּן הַכֹּל.
— which embodies the illumination of King Messiah who will rectify all.
וְכֵן עִנְיַן יוֹסֵף שֶׁגָּדַר עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעֶרְוָה
— And likewise the matter of Joseph who fenced himself against immorality
וְנִגְדְּרוּ כָּל הַזְּכָרִים בִּזְכוּתוֹ
— and all males in Egypt were walled against licentiousness in his merit
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד, כה),
— (as written in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:25),
וְהוּא הֲכָנָה לִגְאוּלַּת מִצְרַיִם וּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה.
— and this was the vital preparation for the Exodus from Egypt and the Giving of the Torah.

p: וְכֵן שַׁבָּת בְּרָזָא דִּבְרִית
— And so too Shabbat embodies the mystical secret of the Covenant,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
— as written in the holy Zohar,
דְּשַׁבָּת מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא
— for Shabbat is a foretaste of the World to Come
שֶׁאָז יִתְבָּרֵר: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים",
— wherein it will be clarified: “And your people are all righteous,”
כָּל מַאן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִיקְרֵי צַדִּיק,
— for everyone who is circumcised is called righteous,
וְהַזְּמַן בְּשַׁבָּת לְתַקֵּן הַפְּגָם הַזֶּה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַגּוּף בְּשַׂר קֹדֶשׁ.
— and Shabbat is the auspicious time to rectify this flaw so that the body becomes holy flesh.
וְלָכֵן יֵשׁ מִצְוָה לְעַנֵּג אֶת הַגּוּף,
— Therefore there is a positive mitzvah to delight the physical body,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
— and as the holy Ari of blessed memory wrote
שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת, אַף אִם אוֹכֵל לַהֲנָאַת הַגּוּף, הוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
— that on Shabbat, even if one eats for bodily pleasure, it is likewise elevated in holiness.
רַק מַעֲלַת הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ,
— Only that the preeminent virtue of one who delights the Sabbath is as we noted,
כְּשֶׁמְּכַוֵּין לְעַנֵּג אֶת הַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת שַׁבָּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
— when he intends to delight the additional soul which is termed Shabbat as written in the holy Zohar,
וְאָז זוֹכֶה לְכָל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קיח עַמּוּדִים א–ב):
— and then he merits all that they proclaimed in the Gemara (Shabbat 118a–b):
שֶׁנּוֹתְנִין לוֹ מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבּוֹ וְנַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים.
— that he is granted his heart’s desires and an unbounded heritage.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chukas 2:1: “The essence is to repair the ruin of the serpent, which brought death to the world. The ruin of the serpent began with eating, into which he brought desire and the sensation of self-gratification; afterwards he came upon Chavah and cast filth into her (Shabbat 146a), and from this branched out the hundred and thirty years mentioned in the Gemara (Eruvin 18b), which is the husk of desire. … The repair of the serpent’s ruin is through eating, and therefore eating is called by the term chok, as it says, ‘Feed me my allotted bread (lechem chuki)’: when one knows that Hashem is the One who feeds and sustains, the eating is in holiness, and then holiness is engraved in the heart to repair the ruin of the serpent. This is what the Mechilta says: ‘Chok and mishpat—chok is Shabbat,’ for on Shabbat eating is in holiness, since it is a mitzvah, and through the Shabbat meal one also repairs the ruin of the serpent. … On Shabbat no punishments are needed; only through the delight of Shabbat one merits to repair the ruin of the serpent that was through eating, for everything a person eats on Shabbat is a mitzvah and is called ‘my allotted bread.’”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Chukas 2 gives the reason behind the Arizal’s statement that eating on Shabbat is holy even when it is for bodily pleasure: because eating on Shabbat is itself a mitzvah, Shabbat delight alone repairs the serpent’s ruin, with no need for suffering. It adds the Mechilta’s identification of Shabbat as chok, the “allotted bread” whose holiness is engraved in the heart.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Et HaOchel §8: “Through one food and one meal during the week—or a Shabbat meal—which a person eats with the proper intention for the honor of Heaven and to elevate the powers of the animal soul to the blessed God, all his foods and meals are elevated. This resembles what the masters of the hidden wisdom said about prayer: through one prayer he raises all the defective prayers of the entire year. … Likewise, anyone who awakens even once can elevate all the permitted and optional deeds he performed previously—and certainly the mitzvot performed without intention and vitality—by performing that deed another time with vitality and intention for the sake of Heaven. This is especially so with eating, which resembles offerings, to which the law of one drawing another after it applies, as stated in Shabbat. One act of eating draws another after it to become like itself.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Rav Tzadok gives the intention in holy eating a retrospective reach: a meal directed toward Heaven can awaken the holiness concealed in earlier permitted meals. The Shabbat meal described here therefore does more than sanctify the present bodily pleasure; it can elevate the person’s eating beyond Shabbat as well.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 118a–b: “Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Yosei’s name: Anyone who delights in Shabbat is given an inheritance without bounds, as it is said, “Then you shall delight in Hashem, and I shall cause you to ride upon the heights of the earth, and I shall feed you the inheritance of Jacob your father.” Not like Abraham, of whom it is written, “Arise, walk through the land, its length”; nor like Isaac, of whom it is written, “For to you and your offspring I shall give all these lands”; but like Jacob, of whom it is written, “You shall spread out westward, eastward, northward, and southward.” … Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: Anyone who delights in Shabbat is granted the desires of his heart, as it is written, “Delight yourself in Hashem, and He will give you the desires of your heart.” I do not know what this delight is. When it says, “You shall call Shabbat a delight,” you must say that it means the delight of Shabbat.”
